title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World
author: Yijiang Li, Bingyang Wang, Nuno Vasconcelos
description: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Instead of providing multi-view images, videos, or 3D representations to the model, we preserve the native visual encoding of VLMs, i.e., a single image, one at a time, just like humans, and treat the 3D representation only…
summary: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question.
takeaways: Across six 3D benchmarks, our model ACT3D achieves an average accuracy of 53.2% that improves its base Qwen model by 22.0% and surpasses proprietary Gemini 3.6 Flash.
Following an initial trajectory-supervised finetuning, we apply reinforcement learning (RL) with rewards driven primarily by final-answer correctness.
Instead, the model must learn an effective exploration policy solely from the extent to which its interactions improve performance.
